title: Respond to a data breach
summary: In the first hours, contain the breach and preserve the evidence. In the first days, get counsel and count deadlines. Every US state has its own breach-notification law (the NCSL survey maps them), some with deadlines in days: California now sets a hard clock (law rule us-ca.breach-notification-timing, residents within 30 calendar days of discovery). Which laws apply depends on where the affected people live, not where your company is. You cannot unsend a notification, so work out the scope first, then notify whoever the statutes require, with counsel. The geo notes cover the non-US equivalents: the UK GDPR's 72-hour ICO deadline, Germany's Article 33 state authorities, India's six-hour CERT-In directions, New Zealand's serious-harm notification to the Privacy Commissioner (law rule nz.privacy-breach-notification), and Australia's notifiable data breaches scheme (law rule au.notifiable-data-breaches: assess within 30 days, then notify the OAIC and affected individuals as soon as practicable). Educational guidance, not legal advice. These deadlines are statutes; verify each against the relevant state's law with counsel.

parts.title: Contain the breach: revoke compromised credentials, rotate keys, isolate affected systems

execution.rationale: The incident team uses the actual security and infrastructure controls to revoke credentials, rotate secrets and isolate affected systems under incident authority.

parts.title: Preserve the forensic evidence: logs, disk images, access records — nothing gets wiped

execution.rationale: The incident responder preserves logs, access records and forensic images through the actual digital evidence systems, maintaining provenance and avoiding destructive changes.

parts.title: Assemble the incident timeline and scope: what data, whose, how many records

execution.rationale: Reconcile supplied incident records into an evidenced timeline and affected-data scope, preserving unknown counts.

parts.title: Engage breach counsel (and your cyber-insurance carrier's hotline if you're covered)

execution.rationale: The incident owner contacts breach counsel and the carrier through the supported remote channels and shares only authorized incident information.

parts.title: Map the notification clocks: every jurisdiction where affected people live can have its own breach statute — some clocks run in hours or days

metadata.trigger: You discover unauthorized access to customer or company data: a breach is live or just happened.
metadata.supportReason: Containment calls, counsel, statute mapping, and the notifications themselves are human judgment with legal weight. An agent can preserve the forensic evidence and assemble the incident timeline; it cannot decide who must be told what, where.

geoNotes.summary: Under UK GDPR a notifiable personal-data breach must be reported to the ICO without undue delay and within 72 hours of awareness — the ICO's self-assessment and reporting flow is the canonical route.

In Germany GDPR Article 33 applies — report to the competent state data-protection authority within 72 hours of awareness; the federal BfDI fronts the supervisory landscape and routes to the Länder authorities.

India's CERT-In directions require reporting covered cyber incidents within six hours of noticing — far tighter than any US state clock — and the DPDP Act adds personal-data-breach duties toward the Data Protection Board.

GDPR Article 33 in France runs through the CNIL: notify within 72 hours of awareness via the CNIL's online breach-notification teleservice (a two-stage notification is allowed while facts are incomplete), and inform the affected people where the risk to them is high.

GDPR Article 33 applies directly: report a notifiable personal-data breach to the CNPD within 72 hours of awareness and notify affected individuals when the risk is high — the CNPD fronts the national reporting flow.

Under PIPEDA, report breaches posing a real risk of significant harm to the Privacy Commissioner, notify affected individuals, and keep records of every breach for 24 months — Quebec's private-sector law adds its own CAI reporting track.
geoNotes.actionLabel: OPC — respond to a privacy breach

geoNotes.summary: A breach that has caused, or is likely to cause, anyone serious harm must be notified to the Privacy Commissioner and affected people as soon as practicable (Privacy Act 2020) — the Commissioner's NotifyUs tool is the channel, ideally within 72 hours.

The PDPA clock is concrete: assess suspected breaches expeditiously, notify the PDPC no later than 3 calendar days after assessing a breach notifiable (law rule sg.pdpa-breach-notification), then notify affected individuals of significant-harm breaches.

The Privacy Act's notifiable data breaches scheme (law rule au.notifiable-data-breaches): assess a suspected eligible breach within 30 days, then give the OAIC a statement and notify affected individuals as soon as practicable — the OAIC's online NDB form is the channel. Small business operators under the $3 million turnover threshold are generally outside the scheme.
